page: Microsoft Azure E48ads_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on AMD EPYC 9V74 processors utilizing the x86_64 architecture. Managed via Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance supplies 48 dedicated virtual CPUs across 24 physical cores running at 3.7 GHz with simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation totals 384 GB of RAM, sustaining an 8 GB per vCPU ratio. Hardware includes 2,832 GB of local NVMe SSD temporary storage, while hardware-accelerated GPUs and complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong compute and in-memory processing capabilities across the board. The instance achieves top-quartile performance in stress-ng single-core and multi-core evaluations, alongside a Geekbench multi-core rating of 20,385 and a PassMark CPU score of 62,946.61. Architectural support for AVX-512, VAES, and SHA-NI enhances cryptographic and vectorized tasks, reflected in a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 310.75 GB/sec and top-tier small-model LLM generation reaching 333.37 tokens per second. Caching throughput is robust at 3,648.86 GB/sec for small blocks, whereas large uncached reads and writes level off at 114.93 GB/sec and 83.19 GB/sec.

The combination of dedicated AMD EPYC execution threads, a 1:8 core-to-memory footprint, and fast integrated NVMe storage makes this configuration cost-efficient for heavy data footprints. Benchmarks show 67.13 million Redis SET operations per second and strong PassMark database results, though the lack of discrete GPUs limits viability for heavy LLM inference workloads exceeding 70B parameters. The instance delivers optimal resource efficiency for enterprise databases, Redis caching layers, in-memory analytics engines, and large-scale compilation pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure E48ads_v6 is a memory-optimized instance featuring 48 dedicated vCPUs (24 physical cores) powered by a 3.7 GHz AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. Built on x86_64 architecture, the configuration pairs 384 GB of system RAM with 2,832 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, achieving an 8 GB per vCPU allocation ratio without bundled GPUs. Benchmark metrics demonstrate top-quartile performance across stress-ng multi-core execution, PassMark CPU testing, and multi-threaded decompression. Database and memory subsystem workloads perform exceptionally well, posting 67.13 million Redis SET operations per second alongside high-throughput cached memory transfers. Uncached memory bandwidth and web serving settle in the mid-range tier, and large-scale model inference shows typical CPU constraints. The server delivers high hardware density and qualitative efficiency for in-memory databases, large data analysis, software build systems, and demanding transaction processing engines.
